source_head_policy: Latest commit returned by GitHub commit search during this review. A commit pin proves provenance only, not safety.

repositories.use: TypeScript/JavaScript technical-indicator implementations for independent formula comparison only.
risks: Latest repository commit surfaced is 2020-03-16; npm 3.1.0 was published years ago.
Legacy TypeScript 2.x and older build/test dependencies require compatibility and supply-chain review.
Indicator names such as VWAP/OBV/volume profile do not establish valid traded volume for Deriv synthetic indices.

repositories.use: Backtrader-based research/backtesting framework with strategies, market-data fetchers, CLI and MCP server; evaluate architecture and test methodology only.
risks: GPL-3.0 compatibility must be resolved before any code reuse or distribution.
Broad dependencies include data-provider, numerical, plotting and MCP packages.
No evidence yet of Deriv synthetic-index data fidelity, contract/cost modelling, no-lookahead validation or reproducible out-of-sample results.

repositories.use: React 19+/StyleX design system; potentially useful only as a separate UI design reference.
risks: Not a trading, risk, execution or research capability.
Repository is very large; no reason to clone or import it into the trading runtime.

repositories.use: Native Rust CLI for AI-driven browser automation and accessibility-tree interaction.
risks: Node.js 22+ and native binary/browser installation are required.
Browser control can reach authenticated sessions if misconfigured; use disposable profiles and synthetic logins only.
Review launcher, postinstall, browser permissions, downloads, network egress and credential storage before execution.

repositories.license_observed: No LICENSE file found at repository root during this review
repositories.use: Agent skill that audits a codebase and writes implementation plans; README describes optional dispatch/execution of plans by other agents.
risks: No root LICENSE or package.json was found in the inspected paths; clarify licensing and complete tree contents.
Execution/dispatch modes and optional GitHub issue publishing expand agent write permissions.
Review the complete skill prompt and subagent/worktree controls before any installation.

repositories.use: Engineering lifecycle skills for spec, plan, build, test, review, web performance, simplify and ship workflows.
risks: Commands such as /build auto and /ship can trigger multi-step implementation or release work.
Review each skill's tools, hooks, file/network access and approval boundaries before enabling it.
Do not allow skill instructions to override AURELIA release authority or independent review.

repositories.use: Codex Security CLI, TypeScript SDK and GitHub Action for source scanning, finding validation, patch proposals and reports.
risks: CLI/CI usage requires an API key or Codex Security credential; do not expose production secrets to scanner jobs.
Review source upload, cloud processing, retention, telemetry, report publishing and permissions before scanning proprietary AURELIA code.
Security findings require human/independent validation; scanner output cannot approve its own patches or releases.

repositories.use: Educational Java algorithm and data-structure implementations; consult for concepts only.
risks: Not a trading strategy library or validated quantitative implementation.
Do not port algorithms into production without independent mathematical specification, tests and performance review.
Repository targets Java 21 and includes test/build dependencies; no runtime need established.

repositories.use: GitHub JavaScript Action that obtains penv-cloud secrets through GitHub OIDC and supplies them only to a specified command process.
repositories.recommended_ref_policy: Pin full 40-character commit SHA only after complete source review; upstream README explicitly rejects mutable tags.
risks: Action executes a command with external secrets in its process environment.
Upstream action.yml/README explicitly state it does not protect against a malicious step in the same job; revocation is best-effort and short server TTL is a separate control.
Only README, action.yml, package.json, main.mjs and post.mjs were inspected; api/delivery/revocation implementation and complete tests remain unaudited.
Do not add duplicate action steps; do not add to AURELIA production CI or deliver Deriv/broker/production credentials.

limitations: This is a metadata/README/licence and selected-entrypoint first-pass review, not a complete source or security audit.
No repository code or action was executed; no SBOM, vulnerability, malware, secret or dynamic sandbox test was produced.
The penv-run action's api/deliver/revoke implementation and complete test suite remain to be inspected.
Assignments route future review only; they do not prove agent runtimes are connected or participated.
